finding: The $1.2-1.4B AI-native break-even is the floor of a plausible range, not its centre. Each plausible omission is small; together they move F5 standalone from $1.39B to ~$2.0B and F3 from $1.45B to ~$2.1B.
reproduction: [M] adv/scripts/experiments.fsx -> adv/work/experiments.out E14: F5 standalone $1.39B -> +$320k fixed (sales to $250k +$188k, independent reconciliation reviewer +$40k, turnover/recruiting +$40k, replacement-sponsor onboarding +$52k) $1.57B -> + MSP at 1.5x and LYR Echelon reliance ($300k x 90%) $1.74B -> + half of December excess carried by employees $1.99B; F3: $1.45B -> $1.65B -> $1.82B -> $2.08B. Outcome-designed F5 with the first two adjustments $1.59B.
effect: Headline break-even moves from $1.2-1.4B to about $1.6-2.0B (F5), overlapping the previous study's fully loaded $1.8-2.3B.
fix: Publish the range with every adjustment as an explicit switch (Sales, Reviewer, Turnover, ChurnOnboarding, BuildMultiple, EchelonReliance, DecemberEmployeeShare). Present $1.2-1.4B only as 'if all favourable assumptions hold'.

finding: Designs.fs labels the LYR pass's base platform as 'conservative' (lyrLayers) and uses a much lighter baseLayers for every headline: Echelon $150k x 30% = $45k vs LYR $0.27M caused + 40% usage share; maintenance $300k vs LYR lead + 3 engineers $789k. The two passes assume different scope (DEV minimum servicing product with 1-2 engineers vs full Unbound initial scope). The headline picks the light one without saying so.
reproduction: [M] model/out/results.md section 13: F5 standalone base $1.39B vs LYR $2.22B; [M] E08: base layers with only LYR Echelon reliance $1.52B. LYR report part 1: group break-even $2.3-2.8B base.
effect: Break-even $1.39B (base) vs $2.22B (LYR); the capital trough in sequences rises by $3-5M with the LYR platform (E06).
fix: Do not call LYR 'conservative'. Label both as bases for different scopes (MSP + 1-2 engineers vs full scope + 4 engineers). Reconcile the Echelon charge: LYR's second maintainer is avoidable only if no Echelon runtime component ships to production. Pessimism caution: the 4-engineer LYR team is sized for 1,185 normative items, not the MSP.

finding: evaluateDesign buys any December excess as premium hours (+50%) with no capacity limit. OPS finds that above ~5,000 accounts December, not annual hours, sets core headcount: temps cannot release, and CNV-GOV-004 makes pre-contracted surge reviewers sponsor-appointed and exclusive to one sponsor. At 10,000 accounts OPS needs 15 servicing FTE (50.7 min) or 9 (30 min) on December sizing, against 5-8 on annual sizing.
reproduction: [M] E04: F5 at $2.5B (10,000 accounts) = 8 employees + 2.4 contracted FTE, peak cost $0.13M. Covering half the excess with employees adds $0.50M/yr; all of it adds $1.01M. Operating break-even: $1.12B -> $1.28B (half) -> $1.48B (all); F3 $1.09B -> $1.25B -> $1.47B. OPS report part 3/4.
effect: +$0.16-0.36B on operating break-even; +$0.2-1.0M/yr in cost at $1-2.5B.
fix: Add a December constraint: release-capable capacity >= December release demand / monthly capacity, with a parameter for the prep-only share that temps can do. Price surge reviewers as per-sponsor retainers.

finding: controlCheck accepts two authorised people plus a contracted reconciliation reviewer (F3). CNV-GOV-003 requires three distinct persons for release until the external auditor and the board accept the deterministic gate. It also requires reconciliation outside the payment chain. In F3, F5 and F6 the controller both releases (MoneyAuthority=true) and sits in the accounting pool, which does reconciliation. F3's third person, and its absence cover, is the sponsor's appointee: transferred, not eliminated.
reproduction: [S] unbound/requirements/convergence/2026-11-24-master/data/convergence-clauses.jsonl CNV-GOV-003 statement; Designs.fs f3/f5 (controller money=true, pool accounting); Design.fs controlCheck. Model note for F3 at $1B: 'absence of either suspends release to the sponsor-appointed authority'.
effect: Small direct cost (+$40k/yr reviewer for F5/F6; F3 needs outsourced reconciliation, +$24-60k). Large effect on the claim: the '3-person minimum safe organisation' is safe only with a sponsor-provided third person and release suspended on absence.
fix: Count distinct persons per payment (preparer, approver, releaser) before acceptance. Require the reconciler to be outside the payment chain. Report sponsor-provided persons as transferred work. Add a reviewer to F5/F6.

finding: Sections 2-3 and design-breakeven.csv report break-even and margins for F1 and F2 even though their controlCheck is NO. They cannot operate with live money. Their rows are the lowest in the tables ($0.84-1.01B operating), so they are easy to quote out of context.
reproduction: model/out/results.md section 3: F1 at 10 min $840M operating; section 2: F1 'NO: ... single point of failure'. [M] E01.
effect: Risk of a sub-$1B headline taken from inadmissible designs. Among feasible designs the floor is F3 at $1.09B operating and F5 at $1.39B standalone.
fix: Mark F1/F2 as 'pre-launch build organisations only' and drop them from break-even outputs, or print 'not admissible with live money' in every row.

finding: Sequences charge the one-off build but no recurring platform cost: Echelon's Unbound share, non-production and CI environments, servicing-specific platform, or the maintenance gap after go-live (maintenance $300k less embedded engineering; F3's CTO covers $167k of it). The annual standalone view includes these lines, so the capital and break-even figures are inconsistent.
reproduction: [M] E06 (recurring from formation; maintenance and servicing-specific from first go-live): capital A $11.44M->$11.99M, B $5.39M->$5.71M, C $5.19M->$5.48M, D $6.14M->$6.49M, E $6.22M->$7.35M, F $3.75M->$4.32M, G $5.88M->$6.30M; with LYR layers F $7.22M, B $9.18M. Year-5 profit for F falls by about $0.23M/yr (gap $133k + $99k), which E06 does not show because OneTime is excluded from accrued profit.
effect: Capital $3.7-6.2M becomes $4.3-7.4M (base layers), or $7.2-11.2M with LYR layers.
fix: Add the Layer A/B recurring lines to Sequence.Recurring, the maintenance gap from go-live.

finding: Every sequence uses the minimum servicing product at 2x ($1.70M), including D and G through extensionBuild and narrowBuild. DEV's planning range is 1.5-3x with 1x as the downside; 2x is 'consistent with Echelon's raw output but not with any measured accepted-capability rate'; Rehearsal 4 (1 of 108 P0 passed) contradicts 5x and above.
reproduction: [M] E06 'MSP at 1x': B $5.39M->$6.35M, C $5.19M->$6.12M, E $6.22M->$7.37M, F $3.75M->$4.71M; E07 MSP 1x $2.43M, 1.5x $1.94M, 2x $1.70M, 3x $1.45M. DEV report 'Productivity sensitivities'.
effect: +$0.2-1.0M of capital at 1.5-1x; the failure modifier (build x2) is the only coverage.
fix: Set the base at 1.5x and treat 2-3x as upside to be earned by the DEV measurement protocol. Parameterise D/G builds on the same multiple.

finding: The minimum servicing product is 44.2% of conventional scope, and DEV defers 17 capabilities, some by moving labour to operations or sponsors: manual custodian import, scripted migration, manual SOC evidence, sponsor staff approving. Sequences nonetheless apply the full-automation 50-minute target 12 months after first go-live. The deferred 56% of scope ($1.86M at 2x) is never funded within 60 months.
reproduction: Designs.fs unboundBaseline MinimumScopeShare=0.442; dev/deferrable-capabilities.csv; Sequences.fs baseSeq Target=50 with RedesignLagMonths=12; failure-costs.csv 'handling stays AI-enhanced' +$0.18-1.50M capital.
effect: Handling cost understated while scope is deferred: up to $0.33M/yr at $1B (F5: 100 min $2.51M vs 50 min $2.18M, section 4). Deferred build of $1.55-2.79M (3x-1x) is outside the plan.
fix: Tie Target to delivered scope (scope-to-minutes map). Add the deferred build as a scheduled outlay triggered by sponsor count or scale.

finding: 'Capital required' is the cash trough including 10%/yr financing on the negative balance. Year-5 profit excludes financing. ROIC = after-tax (21%) year-5 accrued profit / trough. That mixes equity and debt. If the capital is equity, the trough is overstated. If it is debt, year-5 profit omits interest on a balance still negative at month 60 (B -$4.80M, about $0.48M/yr of interest against $0.82M profit). ROIC is a single-year snapshot with no terminal value, no time value and no loss carryforward.
effect: The capital headline is 16-24% overstated as equity need (pessimistic), or year-5 profit is ~40-60% overstated if the capital is debt (optimistic). The ROIC ranking is unaffected; its level is not meaningful.
fix: Report the equity need (financing 0) and the debt case separately. Replace ROIC with NPV/IRR over 5-10 years with an explicit terminal value and NOL usage.

finding: The 'Combined software + administration' scenario allocates 50% of Unbound to external licensees who do not exist. It adds no licence sales, licensee SOC 2 or support cost, and ignores the $300k external revenue. It produces the lowest break-even in the matrix. LYR estimates a captive platform needs ~19-21k external funds at $91/fund.
reproduction: [M] E08: F5 fully allocated at 3x, servicing share 1.0 $1.35B vs 0.5 $1.15B. model/out/results.md section 13. LYR report finding 1.
effect: $0.20B of break-even rests on cost borne by hypothetical customers.
fix: Allocate platform cost to licensees only with modelled licensee revenue, licensee acquisition (~$250k/yr sales) and SOC 2 scope. Otherwise drop the row.

finding: The model's own bridge shows the 'different company' is mostly a different build-cost and sales assumption, not a different organisation. At $1.5B, of the $1.08M fall from the previous fully loaded Model B ($3.88M) to F5 standalone ($2.80M), $0.26M comes from workload-driven staffing. About $0.81M comes from replacing $1.0M build amortisation and $250k sales with a $0.44M platform charge and $62k of sales lines.
reproduction: model/out/results.md section 12 (bridge rows); Designs.fs salesAndGa.
effect: About 75% of the claimed improvement is an unmeasured 2x build multiple and lower sales spend. Without them the organisation saves ~$0.26M/yr, about $0.08B of break-even.
fix: State the attribution in the headline. Carry the build multiple and sales as the first two sensitivities.

finding: 21 of 26 Echelon repos are PolyForm Noncommercial, and CNV-GOV-009 bars them from release 1 without a commercial licence. The base model carries $0. The only coverage is a $60k/yr failure modifier, while LYR's cost-plus transfer price is $0.13-0.67M/yr. The licence is a launch blocker, not a sensitivity.
reproduction: dev/report.jsonl summary (licence row); lyr/report.jsonl part 1 T01; Sequences.fs echelonLicence ($5k/month).
effect: Unknown cost; launch blocked until resolved. Each $100k/yr adds ~$65M of break-even (LYR rule of thumb).
fix: Put a licence line in the base (owner-set). Add a gate: no go-live without an executed licence or replacement code.

finding: Coordination of 0.5 h per pair per week is added on top of 1,520 productive hours, which already deduct ~15% for meetings and admin (previous report 03; OPS part 5). This double counts, and errs towards pessimism.
reproduction: [M] E02: F5 break-even $1.12B->$1.10B; F8 $1.31B->$1.27B; F3 unchanged; coordination cost at $1.5B F5 $0.04M.
effect: -$0.00-0.04B of break-even (model too pessimistic).
fix: Count coordination only above the deducted baseline (e.g. pairs beyond 6), or raise productive hours when coordination is explicit.

finding: outcomeDesigned raises ProductiveHours by 3%, but the added-capacity cost is FTE x ProductiveHours x (Loaded/1,520). Each employee then costs 3% more ($102,462 vs $99,478), and fractional capacity cost does not change, so the coordination gain cancels.
reproduction: [M] E03: total cost with vs without +3% differs by <= $0.01M at $1-5B; E11 implied per-employee cost 102,462 vs 99,478.
effect: The outcome-designed gain from coordination (~$33k/yr per OPS) is lost. The model is slightly pessimistic here.
fix: Cost hires at Pool loaded cost per FTE, independent of productive hours. Model productivity as queue hours.

finding: The outcome-designed variant (30.1 min; 12,720 sponsor minutes) rightly excludes transferred work from servicer cost. But no output reports the 5.0 min/account and 600 min/sponsor-year moved to donors, charities, intermediaries, sponsors and auditors. S04's -1,100 min depends on auditor reliance (CNV-GOV-001), and the 45-75 minute pre-delegation year per sponsor is ignored. Its $1.24B is shown beside the designs with only an '[unproven]' tag.
reproduction: ops/report.jsonl part 2 (transfers), part 1 (pre-delegation); Designs.fs outcomeDesigned; model/out/results.md section 13 row 9.
effect: Servicer cost is fine. System cost is understated by ~$22k/yr of labour at $1B, plus unquantified fund-borne intermediary fees. Sponsor willingness to pay is affected.
fix: Print a transferred-work ledger beside the variant. Gate the variant on auditor and board acceptance. Apply per-sponsor pre-delegation.

finding: EarlyTarget (~100 min) applies only for 12 months after the FIRST go-live. OPS says every new sponsor starts in pre-delegation (three-person release, 100% calibration, +~14 min; 45-75 min in year 1).
reproduction: Sequences.fs targetAt; [M] E12 RedesignLagMonths 24 as a proxy: B capital $5.39M->$5.71M, F $3.75M->$4.05M.
effect: +$0.3M capital; year-5 profit lower whenever sponsors are added late.
fix: Set the target per sponsor by months since that sponsor's go-live.

finding: narrowEntryNonPersonnel drops CST-C04 (compliance consultant: sanctions, due diligence, independent review) from a service whose product is charity verification and screening. COM says to sell only after sanctions recall is fixed (88/100 in the public replay). It keeps the payment-release reviewer and two code approvers, although no money moves. Six sponsors at $40k are assumed with no demand evidence; COM calls the category commoditised.
reproduction: Designs.fs narrowEntryNonPersonnel; Sequences.fs seqD/seqG OtherIncome; com/report.jsonl part 2 (charity verification row).
effect: Assurance mis-scoped (+$25k missing, -$40k unneeded). Sequence D/G revenue of $240k/yr is speculative; at zero narrow revenue D's capital rises by ~$0.2M/yr of service life.
fix: Keep C04 and E&O sized for screening liability; drop the payment reviewer pre-administration. Add a zero-demand case.

finding: servicingOnly moves engineers and 'engineering' contracts to Layer B but keeps 'contracted independent code approvers' ($45-90k) in the servicing layer, while Layer B maintenance pays for the code they approve. This duplicates or misallocates the cost.
reproduction: [M] E09: F3 servicingOnly keeps 'contracted independent code approvers x2'; F5 keeps x1.
effect: $45-90k/yr in the wrong layer; incremental/FA servicing cost overstated by that amount.
fix: Move code approvers to Layer B (CNV-PLT-010 is a platform control).

finding: Layer charges enter as a constant ExtraordinaryCost computed at the $1B reference. That is correct for fixed lines. But integration upkeep that servicingOnly makes fractional, and per-sponsor platform cost, are frozen at 5 sponsors. The same channel also carries incident stresses, so a recurring cost is labelled 'extraordinary' and the two add silently.
reproduction: [M] E10: standalone charge $0.44M and FA charge $0.74M, identical at $0.5B, $1B and $3B; Program.fs charge/withCharge.
effect: Negligible at 5 sponsors; wrong for any sponsor-count or stress sensitivity.
fix: Add a PlatformCharge field computed per evaluation from the sponsor list.

finding: The test 'layer views order incremental below fully allocated below standalone' never asserts fully allocated < standalone, and it compares F5 fully allocated with F3 standalone. For F3, fully allocated ($2.716M) actually exceeds standalone ($2.715M).
reproduction: tests/CapitalMinimization.Tests/Tests.fs:112-120; model/out/results.md section 7: F3 profit -$716k FA vs -$715k standalone.
effect: None on the numbers; the test name misstates what is verified.
fix: Assert per design. Document that FA can exceed standalone because Layer-B engineering is bought fractionally at a premium.

finding: Hiring happens at floor(need + 0.25), i.e. once residual need reaches 0.75 FTE. F3's pools are Fractional, so it never hires: at its standalone break-even ($1.45B) it is 3 employees plus 4.2 contracted FTE, and 7.3 contracted FTE at $3B. The '3-person organisation' is ~7 FTE doing work on charitable money, mostly contractors at a 1.5x premium. The availability of vetted, December-capable fractional staff is not evidenced.
effect: Cost is counted, but the headcount claim is misleading. Access control and SoD over contractors is unpriced.
fix: Report total FTE (employees + contracted). Cap the contracted share of payment-chain work. Let F3 hire above a threshold.

finding: Sales lines are $62k (events, marketing, CRM) plus 30% of the founder; the previous study and LYR carry $250k. No time budget checks that the founder's queue share, MD role, 30% selling, governance and relationship work fit in one person.
reproduction: Designs.fs salesAndGa; Program.fs cacSection; [M] E08: F5 standalone $1.39B -> $1.50B with sales at $250k.
effect: +$0.11B of break-even at $250k sales.
fix: Carry sales at $62-250k. Add a per-person time-budget check (sum of roles <= 1 FTE).

finding: Annual break-even omits replacement-sponsor onboarding (churn), recruiting and turnover, and the expected incident loss. They appear only in sequences or stresses.
reproduction: Design.fs evaluateDesign total; Parameters onboardingBase $105k.
effect: +$0.1-0.2M/yr (churn ~0.5 sponsor/yr x $105k, turnover ~$40k, expected loss $25-100k): ~+$0.07-0.13B of break-even.
fix: Add amortised steady-state lines.

finding: Break-even assumes 5 equal sponsors at a $250k balance and 20 bps. COM finds 20 bps value-defensible only for small/mid-balance or already-outsourced books; equivalent-scope value is 5-10 bps for $1M+ books. F5 at 7 bps never breaks even below $3.3B.
reproduction: model/out/results.md section 11; com/report.jsonl part 1e; [M] E14 adjusted F5 at 15 bps $3.02B.
effect: The headline is valid only inside the segment where 20 bps holds, which is a handful of decision units (previous ADV-002).
fix: Attach the segment condition to every break-even. Show break-even under COM's per-account tariff at segment balances.

finding: PreLaunchFixedShare 0.4 scales all non-personnel before the first go-live. But the SOC 1 Type 2 observation must start before the first staffed client goes live (OD-P-GOV), the pen test must precede live money, and insurance must be bound before contract.
reproduction: Sequences.fs baseSeq PreLaunchFixedShare; unbound convergence OD-P-GOV decision text.
effect: ~+$50-100k of capital in the 6 months before go-live.
fix: Schedule the assurance and insurance lines explicitly by month.

finding: Sponsor-retained time is 2.7 sponsor-appointed min/account-year in OPS but 7.0 sponsor-retained min/account-year in COM (A-COM-007). The model carries neither.
reproduction: ops/report.jsonl summary; com/assumptions.jsonl A-COM-007.
effect: The buyer-side cost differs by 2.6x between passes, which affects value-based price.
fix: Reconcile into one sponsor-retained activity list and report it as transferred cost.

finding: Failure modifiers are applied one at a time, but the failures are correlated: low productivity, slow sales and unreduced review tend to arrive together. The model also gives no detection signal, contingency or recovery cost per failure, which section 19 asks for (LYR's failure-catalogue.csv does give them).
reproduction: [M] E15: B $5.39M -> $11.20M with build x2 + sales 2x (profitable month 54); C $5.19M -> $10.59M; F $3.75M -> $7.65M; G $5.88M -> $11.67M (not profitable within 60 months). Build x2 + assurance + AI-enhanced handling: B $9.40M, F $6.98M.
effect: Two correlated failures double the capital need. A $3.7-6M raise has no buffer for them.
fix: Add joint-failure scenarios and a staged-tranche plan with stop points. Link each modifier to the detection signal and recovery cost in lyr/failure-catalogue.csv.
